searchText: Amazing!! Btw one thing we should discuss at some point is, exactly how much of this should be standardized There are going to be different clients that take different tradeoffs eg. I've advocated the N-server model Because it gives serious improvements over the status quo of "just trusting infura" but it's still simple enough that people are going to be willing to adopt it We don't want to see amazing pure solutions that nobody actually uses because figuring the p2p out is too complicated or whatever But then if you *do* have a node.... Another benefit of the N-server model is that if you lean on the 1-of-N honesty assumption harder, you get a "poor man's TheGraph" Basically a way to answer web3 log queries ("give me all logs between block X and block Y that satisfy topic T") Ask N servers, get the responses, verify their merkle proofs, union them, and stop trusting any server that misses a log in their response
